subject: science
domain: From Molecules to Organisms: Structures and Processes
intro: The body is organized into levels: cells form tissues, tissues form organs, and organs work together as organ systems. These systems are subsystems of the whole body, and they interact. For example, the digestive system breaks food into nutrients, the circulatory system carries those nutrients and oxygen to cells, and the respiratory system brings in oxygen. No system works alone; the body functions because the subsystems cooperate.

items.prompt: Put these levels of organization in order from smallest to largest: organ, cell, organ system, tissue.
How do the digestive and circulatory systems work together to feed the body's cells?

steps: The digestive system breaks food into nutrients.
The circulatory system picks up those nutrients and carries them in the blood.
Blood delivers the nutrients to cells throughout the body.
solution.answer: Digestion releases nutrients, and circulation delivers them to cells.

items.prompt: Why can we call an organ system a 'subsystem' of the body?

steps: The body as a whole is one large system.
Each organ system performs part of the body's work.
So each system is a smaller part, a subsystem, of the whole body.
solution.answer: Because each organ system is a smaller part of the whole-body system.

items.prompt: What do many similar cells form when grouped together?

steps: Groups of similar cells form a tissue.

items.prompt: Name the system that brings oxygen into the body.

steps: The respiratory system takes in oxygen through the lungs.

items.prompt: Give one example of two body systems interacting.

steps: The respiratory system takes in oxygen and the circulatory system carries it to cells.
solution.answer: The respiratory and circulatory systems work together to supply oxygen.
